transcript:
User: This is Frank. Whoever you people are, I want to know how you got this number.
Agent: Got it, Frank — sounds like our call caught you off guard.  

I’m Linda with Dialux; we work with small businesses on missed-call handling — did you get a voicemail from us recently, or did this number just show up on your phone out of the blue?
User: Out of the blue. I don't trust you folks, Dialux or whatever. You people are all liars and thieves.
Agent: I hear you, Frank — if a call feels out of the blue, it’s fair to be skeptical.  

We don’t buy consumer lists; we typically only contact business numbers that came through public business directories or prior business inquiries — is this your business line or your personal cell?
User: That's none of your damn business. Your guarantees ain't worth the paper they're printed on.
Agent: I hear you, Frank — if you’re feeling that strongly, I don’t want to drag this out or bother you.  

I’ll go ahead and make sure we don’t contact this number again; is there anything else you want from us besides stopping the calls?
User: Well. Maybe you're not all crooks. Leave your number, I might look you up.
Agent: Totally fair, Frank — if you ever do want to look us up, the company name is Dialux and you can call this same number that showed up on your phone today to get back to us. Thanks for hearing me out a bit; I’ll make sure we don’t bug you, and I’ll let you go now.

The agent, Linda, clarified the reason for the call, addressed Frank's concerns, and assured him that his number would not be contacted again, providing company information for future reference. The conversation ended with the agent respecting Frank's wishes and ending the call.
